name: Sabanci Holding
desc: Turkish conglomerate holding Akbank, insurance, energy (Enerjisa), cement, retail, tyre cord and other industrial businesses.
markets: Mainly Turkey; industrial units such as Kordsa operate plants and sell in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Large Turkish group with consumer banking and energy brands; F1 hospitality could support corporate profile in Turkey and abroad.

name: TransUnion
desc: Credit reporting agency providing credit reports, scores, identity verification, fraud prevention and marketing data to businesses and consumers.
markets: Credit and data customers in about 30 countries, largest in the US, plus Canada, UK, India, Latin America and Africa.
rationale: Data and analytics brand with B2B client base in US, UK and India; F1 could serve hospitality and tech positioning.
changed: Acquired Neustar in 2021

name: Investec
desc: Specialist bank and wealth manager offering private banking, corporate and investment banking and wealth services to affluent clients.
markets: Main operations in the UK and South Africa, with smaller presence in Europe, India and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Affluent private-banking clientele and established sports sponsorship culture suit F1 hospitality in the UK and South Africa.

name: Halyk Bank
desc: Kazakhstan's largest bank, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, cards, insurance, brokerage and a consumer super-app.
markets: Kazakhstan, with subsidiaries in Kyrgyzstan, Georgia, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan; no verified plans beyond Central Asia and Caucasus.
rationale: Dominant consumer bank in Kazakhstan, but markets lie outside the F1 calendar core; mainly domestic brand building.

name: Société Générale
desc: French universal bank providing retail banking, investment banking, markets, car leasing through Ayvens and asset servicing.
markets: France and Europe core, retail units in Central Europe and Africa, investment banking across the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Global bank where rivals Santander, UBS and Barclays sponsor F1; useful for corporate hospitality and Ayvens mobility link.

name: Woori Financial Group
desc: South Korean financial holding company owning Woori Bank, Woori Card, securities, capital, asset management and insurance units.
markets: Mainly South Korea; Woori Bank runs overseas branches and subsidiaries in Asia, the US and Europe.
rationale: Large Korean consumer financial brand; F1 could support corporate hospitality and Asian expansion, though focus stays domestic.

name: KB Financial Group
desc: South Korean financial holding company owning KB Kookmin Bank, KB Securities, KB Insurance and KB Kookmin Card.
markets: Mainly South Korea; subsidiaries in Indonesia, Cambodia and other Asian markets, plus branches in financial centres.
rationale: Leading Korean consumer finance brand with sports marketing record; F1 fit mainly for corporate hospitality and Asian growth.

name: China International Capital Corporation (CICC)
desc: Chinese investment bank providing underwriting, advisory, brokerage, asset management and wealth management services.
markets: Mostly mainland China clients, with offices in Hong Kong, Singapore, London, New York and other centres.
rationale: Institutional investment bank with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could reach corporate clients but fit is modest.

name: AIG
desc: Global insurer selling commercial, specialty and personal property and casualty insurance to businesses and individuals.
markets: Operates in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions through local insurers and branches.
rationale: Global insurer with past major sports sponsorship; rivals Aon and Marsh partner F1 teams, making B2B hospitality relevant.
changed: Separated life and retirement unit Corebridge Financial from 2022

name: Chubb
desc: Property and casualty insurer providing commercial, personal, specialty, accident and health insurance and reinsurance worldwide.
markets: Operates in over 50 countries across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: High-net-worth personal lines and corporate clients match F1 audience; hospitality and brand reach across global markets.
changed: Formed when ACE acquired Chubb Corp in 2016

name: Zurich Insurance Group
desc: Swiss insurer providing property, casualty and life insurance to individuals, small businesses and large corporations worldwide.
markets: Customers in more than 200 countries and territories, with large businesses in Europe, North America, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global insurance brand already active in sports sponsorship; F1 offers worldwide visibility and corporate hospitality.

name: Howden Group Holdings
desc: Insurance and reinsurance broker placing commercial, specialty, reinsurance and personal cover, also running underwriting agencies.
markets: Operates in many countries across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Fast-growing broker competing with F1 partners Aon and Marsh; strong case for B2B hospitality and global brand building.

name: Travelers
desc: Property and casualty insurer selling commercial, personal auto and home, and specialty insurance through independent agents.
markets: Mainly the United States, with operations in Canada, the UK and Ireland.
rationale: Strong US brand with golf sponsorship; F1 growth in the US offers fit, but international reach is limited.

name: Generali Group
desc: Italian insurer selling life, property and casualty insurance and asset management to individuals and businesses.
markets: Strongest in Italy, France, Germany and Central Europe, with operations in Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Major European consumer brand with sponsorship history; Italian and European F1 races give strong home-market exposure.

name: MAPFRE
desc: Spanish insurer selling motor, home, life, health and commercial insurance, plus reinsurance through MAPFRE RE.
markets: Spain, Brazil, Latin America and the US are main markets, with reinsurance worldwide.
rationale: Motor insurance focus and strong Spanish and Latin American brand suit F1 audiences in Spain, Mexico and Brazil.

name: Nippon Life Insurance Company
desc: Japan's largest life insurer, a mutual company selling life, annuity and health insurance to individuals and companies.
markets: Mainly Japan; overseas life insurance and asset management businesses in the US, Australia, Asia and Europe.
rationale: Strong Japanese consumer brand; Japanese GP hospitality plausible, but domestic focus limits global F1 value.
changed: Acquired full ownership of Resolution Life in 2025

name: SCOR
desc: Global reinsurer providing life, health, property, casualty and specialty reinsurance to insurance companies.
markets: Reinsurance clients in many countries across Europe, the Americas and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B reinsurer with no consumer brand; F1 useful only for client hospitality, so a weak to moderate fit.

name: Tokio Marine
desc: Japanese insurance group selling property, casualty and life insurance, with large specialty insurance businesses in the US.
markets: Japan core market, with major operations in North America, Europe, Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Leading Japanese insurer with large US business; F1 could support global brand and corporate hospitality, especially in Japan.

name: Dai-ichi Life
desc: Japanese life insurance group selling life, annuity and health products, with insurers in the US, Australia and Asia.
markets: Japan, plus Protective in the US, TAL in Australia, and operations in Vietnam, India and other markets.
rationale: Strong Japanese consumer brand with international insurers; F1 could aid brand building in Japan and overseas markets.
changed: Holding company renamed Dai-ichi Life Group in 2025

name: Intact Financial
desc: Canadian property and casualty insurer selling home, auto and business insurance, plus specialty lines in the UK and US.
markets: Canada core, with RSA operations in the UK and Ireland and specialty insurance in the US.
rationale: Leading Canadian auto insurer; Canadian Grand Prix and UK ties give a plausible marketing fit.
changed: Acquired RSA Insurance Group in 2021

name: Liberty Mutual Insurance
desc: Mutual insurer selling auto, home and commercial insurance to individuals and businesses, plus specialty lines worldwide.
markets: Mainly the US, with specialty and commercial insurance operations in Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Big US consumer advertiser with sports sponsorship heritage; growing US F1 audience makes it a credible prospect.

name: Ageas
desc: Belgian insurance group selling life and non-life insurance in Europe and through joint ventures in Asia.
markets: Belgium, UK and Portugal in Europe, with joint ventures in China, India, Thailand and other Asian markets.
rationale: Consumer insurer in Belgium and the UK with Asian growth; F1 plausible for brand building, though not obvious.
changed: Renamed from Fortis Holding in 2010

name: QBE Insurance Group
desc: Australian general insurer and reinsurer selling commercial, specialty, crop and personal insurance.
markets: Operates in about 27 countries across Australia Pacific, North America, the UK and Europe.
rationale: Recognised Australian brand with sports sponsorships; Australian GP and B2B hospitality give a plausible fit.

name: AIA Group
desc: Asia-Pacific life insurer selling life, health, accident and retirement products to individuals and companies.
markets: Operates in 18 markets across Asia-Pacific including Hong Kong, mainland China, Thailand, Singapore and Malaysia; no Europe or Americas business.
rationale: Strong Asian consumer brand with Premier League sponsorship; Asian F1 races in Singapore, China and Japan suit it.
changed: Separated from AIG with Hong Kong IPO in 2010

name: Swiss Re
desc: Swiss reinsurer providing life, health, property and casualty reinsurance and corporate insurance to insurers and businesses.
markets: Around 80 offices in about 29 countries serving clients worldwide.
rationale: B2B reinsurer with limited consumer brand; F1 relevant mainly for client hospitality and risk-themed content.

name: Apollo Global Management
desc: Alternative asset manager investing in credit, private equity and real assets, and owner of retirement insurer Athene.
markets: Investors and portfolio companies across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Rivals Carlyle and other investors sit on the F1 roster; hospitality for limited partners and portfolio companies is plausible.
changed: Merged with Athene Holding in 2022

name: Brookfield Asset Management
desc: Alternative asset manager investing in renewable power, infrastructure, real estate, private equity and credit for institutions.
markets: Investors and assets across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Institutional manager with low consumer awareness; F1 useful for investor hospitality and sustainability messaging only.
changed: Spun off from Brookfield Corporation in 2022

name: BlackRock
desc: Asset manager offering iShares ETFs, active funds, private markets and the Aladdin investment platform to investors.
markets: Offices in about 30 countries and clients in about 100 countries worldwide.
rationale: Global finance brand with institutional clients; iShares retail marketing and hospitality give a plausible F1 case.
changed: Acquired Global Infrastructure Partners in 2024 and Preqin and HPS in 2025

name: Groupama
desc: French mutual insurance group selling car, home, health, life and agricultural insurance to consumers, farmers and businesses.
markets: Mainly France, with operations in about 10 countries such as Italy, Romania, Hungary and Turkey.
rationale: Active French sports sponsor (Groupama-FDJ cycling); French market focus makes F1 plausible but secondary.

name: Prudential Financial
desc: US life insurer and asset manager selling life insurance, annuities, retirement and investment management through PGIM.
markets: Mainly the US, with life insurance in Japan, Brazil and other countries and PGIM investment offices worldwide.
rationale: Well-known US consumer brand with stadium naming; US F1 growth offers a plausible hospitality and marketing case.

name: Principal Financial Group
desc: Financial company providing retirement plans, insurance and asset management to employers, individuals and institutions.
markets: Mainly the US, with retirement and asset management businesses in Latin America and Asia.
rationale: US retirement brand with sport and arts sponsorship; F1 could support US hospitality, but fit is not obvious.

name: MetLife
desc: Insurer selling life insurance, annuities, employee benefits and dental cover to individuals and employers.
markets: Around 90 million customers in over 40 markets, with major businesses in the US, Japan, Latin America and Asia.
rationale: Big consumer brand with long sports sponsorship record; global markets and employer clients suit F1 hospitality.

name: CK Asset Holdings
desc: Hong Kong property group developing and owning real estate, hotels, pubs, aircraft leasing and infrastructure investments.
markets: Property in Hong Kong and mainland China, with investments in the UK, continental Europe, Australia and Canada.
rationale: Mainly B2B property and infrastructure group; F1 fit limited to corporate hospitality in Asia and Europe.

name: Amundi
desc: Asset manager offering funds, ETFs, pension and savings products to retail investors via partners and institutions.
markets: Europe core, with offices and clients in Asia-Pacific, the Americas and the Middle East.
rationale: Europe's largest asset manager with limited consumer brand; F1 could support ETF brand building and client hospitality.

name: Partners Group
desc: Private markets investment manager covering private equity, private credit, infrastructure and real estate for institutions and wealthy investors.
markets: Offices in over 20 cities across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Institutional investment brand; F1 relevant for investor and wealthy-client hospitality, otherwise weak consumer fit.

name: Allianz
desc: German insurer and asset manager selling property, casualty, life and health insurance, and managing assets through PIMCO.
markets: About 70 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Heavy sports sponsor and former F1 partner; global consumer insurance brand with clear motorsport and hospitality fit.

name: Robinhood
desc: Retail investing app offering trading in stocks, ETFs, options, futures, crypto, plus retirement accounts and credit cards.
industry: retail brokerage and crypto trading app
markets: Mainly US retail investors, with crypto and brokerage services in the UK and the EU.
rationale: Young US retail investor base matches F1's growing US fan profile; trading rivals already sponsor F1.
changed: Acquired Bitstamp in 2025

name: Shift4 Payments
desc: Payments processor providing integrated card processing and point-of-sale software to restaurants, hotels, stadiums, retailers and online merchants.
markets: US core, expanding in Europe and worldwide; Global Blue adds tax-free shopping services across Europe and Asia.
rationale: Hospitality and venue payments focus and sports-venue deals make F1 events and partners a natural showcase.
changed: Acquired Global Blue in 2025

name: Euronet Worldwide
desc: Payments company running ATM networks, card processing, epay prepaid services and Ria and Xe money transfer.
markets: Operates in about 200 countries, with large businesses in Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Ria and Xe consumer brands serve global migrant and travel audiences; F1 reach could support remittance marketing.

name: State Street
desc: Custody bank and asset manager providing asset servicing, SPDR ETFs and investment management to institutional investors.
markets: Institutional clients across North America, Europe, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Institutional brand; SPDR ETF marketing and client hospitality give a plausible but not obvious F1 case.

name: Manulife Financial
desc: Insurer and wealth manager selling life and health insurance, retirement and asset management, as John Hancock in the US.
markets: Canada, the US through John Hancock, and many Asian markets; little business in Europe.
rationale: Strong brand in Canada and Asia with sports sponsorship; Asian races and Canadian GP offer a plausible fit.

name: Mitsubishi Corporation
desc: Japanese general trading company with businesses in natural gas, metals, chemicals, mobility, food, power and industrial materials.
markets: Operations and investments in about 90 countries across Asia, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Large B2B conglomerate with mobility and energy interests; F1 could support corporate hospitality and Japanese GP visibility.

name: Sumitomo Corporation
desc: Japanese general trading company with businesses in metals, transport equipment, infrastructure, media, retail and mineral resources.
markets: Operations across Asia, the Americas, Europe, the Middle East and Africa through offices and subsidiaries.
rationale: B2B trading group with automotive and infrastructure interests; F1 fit limited to hospitality and Japanese GP presence.

name: Remitly
desc: Digital remittance company whose app lets migrants send money internationally to bank accounts, wallets and cash pickup.
markets: Senders in the US, Canada, UK, EU, Australia and others, paying out to over 170 countries.
rationale: Consumer brand serving diaspora communities across F1 markets; sports sponsorship history supports a global awareness play.

name: Zepz
desc: Digital money-transfer company running the WorldRemit and Sendwave apps for international remittances to wallets, accounts and cash pickup.
markets: Senders in the UK, Europe, US and Canada, with payouts across Africa, Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Diaspora-focused consumer fintech; F1 is broad reach rather than targeted, so a plausible but uncertain fit.
changed: WorldRemit acquired Sendwave in 2020 and the group was renamed Zepz in 2022

name: Acrisure
desc: Insurance broker and financial services firm offering brokerage, reinsurance, benefits, wealth management and cyber services to businesses.
markets: Mainly the US, with operations in the UK, Europe, Australia and other markets.
rationale: Active stadium sponsor competing with F1 partners Aon and Marsh; B2B hospitality and US F1 growth fit well.

name: Affirm
desc: Buy-now-pay-later lender offering point-of-sale instalment loans and a debit card to shoppers through partnered merchants.
markets: Shoppers in the US, Canada and the UK; no verified wider expansion plans.
rationale: Consumer fintech with sports sponsorship record; US-focused F1 growth and retail partners make it plausible.

name: Nexi
desc: European payments company offering merchant acquiring, card issuing, processing and digital banking infrastructure to banks and merchants.
markets: Italy, the Nordics, the DACH region and Central and Eastern Europe.
rationale: European payments brand at merchant terminals; Italian and European races offer hospitality and visibility, though mostly B2B.
changed: Merged with Nets and SIA in 2021

name: PhonePe
desc: Indian digital payments app built on UPI, offering payments, insurance, investment and lending distribution to consumers and merchants.
industry: UPI payments and financial services app
markets: Customers in India; UPI payments available to Indian travellers in a few foreign markets.
rationale: Huge Indian consumer brand and cricket sponsor, but no Indian GP; F1 reach in India is limited.
changed: Separated from Flipkart in 2022

name: Binance
desc: Cryptocurrency exchange offering spot and derivatives trading, staking, wallets, payments and the BNB Chain ecosystem.
markets: Users worldwide, though restricted or licensed separately in markets such as the US.
rationale: Crypto rivals OKX, Kraken and Crypto.com sponsor F1, but regulatory issues create reputational risk for partners.
changed: Pleaded guilty to US anti-money-laundering violations in 2023

name: Checkout.com
desc: Payments company providing card acquiring, processing, fraud prevention and payouts to large online merchants.
markets: Enterprise merchants across Europe, North America, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Enterprise payments brand competing with F1 partners Stripe and Visa; B2B hospitality and tech showcase fit.

name: Majid Al Futtaim
desc: Emirati group owning shopping malls, Carrefour franchise hypermarkets, VOX Cinemas, Ski Dubai and leisure and hotel assets.
markets: Gulf states, wider Middle East, North Africa and Central Asia.
rationale: Gulf consumer group with high visibility; Middle East races in Abu Dhabi, Qatar and Saudi Arabia fit well.

name: MSCI
desc: Provider of investment indexes, portfolio analytics, ESG ratings and risk models to asset managers, banks and pension funds.
markets: Institutional clients across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B finance data firm with no consumer brand; F1 useful only for client hospitality, a weak fit.

name: Genting Berhad
desc: Malaysian conglomerate operating casino resorts, theme parks and hotels, plus plantations, power and oil and gas.
markets: Resorts World in Malaysia, Singapore, the US and the UK, plantations in Indonesia, power assets abroad.
rationale: Former F1 team sponsor with resorts in F1 host markets such as Singapore, Las Vegas and Malaysia.

name: Ameriprise Financial
desc: Financial planning and wealth management firm with advisors, retirement and insurance products and Columbia Threadneedle asset management.
markets: Mainly US clients via advisors, with Columbia Threadneedle operating in the UK, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Affluent US client base and golf sponsorship; US F1 hospitality is plausible but not an obvious priority.
changed: Spun off from American Express in 2005

name: Ant International
desc: Cross-border digital payments company running Alipay+, Antom merchant payments, WorldFirst business accounts and other fintech services.
markets: Merchants and wallet partners in over 100 markets across Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Global payments network targeting merchants and travellers; rivals Visa and Mastercard sponsor F1, making a case.

name: Great-West Lifeco
desc: Financial holding owning Canada Life, Empower and Irish Life, selling insurance, retirement and wealth management.
markets: Canada, the US through Empower, and Europe through Irish Life and Canada Life UK and Germany.
rationale: Well-known brands in Canada and the US retirement market; F1 plausible for hospitality but not obvious.

name: Swiss Life Group
desc: Swiss provider of life insurance, pensions, financial advice and real estate asset management to individuals and companies.
markets: Customers in Switzerland, France, Germany and other European markets; no verified business outside Europe.
rationale: European insurance brand with sports sponsorship; Swiss and French affluent clients suit F1 hospitality moderately.

name: Finastra
desc: Financial software company supplying lending, payments, corporate banking and digital banking platforms to banks.
markets: Bank clients in more than 100 countries across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: B2B banking software vendor; F1 could support client hospitality and technology positioning, a moderate fit.
changed: Sold its Treasury and Capital Markets business to Apax in 2025

name: Silver Lake
desc: Private equity firm making large technology-focused buyout and growth investments for pension funds and other institutions.
markets: Offices and portfolio companies in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Investor without a consumer brand; F1 relevant only for investor relations or portfolio companies, a weak fit.

name: Arch Capital Group
desc: Bermuda-based specialty insurer and reinsurer writing property, casualty, specialty and mortgage insurance for businesses and insurers.
markets: Operates through about 60 offices across North America, Europe, Australia and Asia, including Lloyd's syndicates.
rationale: B2B specialty insurer with little consumer brand; F1 relevant mainly for broker and client hospitality.

name: Corpay
desc: Corporate payments company providing fleet fuel cards, lodging payments, cross-border and accounts-payable payment services to businesses.
markets: Businesses in the US, UK, Brazil, continental Europe, Australia and other markets.
rationale: Fleet and vehicle payments business with mobility link; B2B hospitality makes F1 a plausible fit.
changed: Renamed from FLEETCOR Technologies in 2024

name: EXOR
desc: Agnelli family investment holding with stakes in Ferrari, Stellantis, CNH, Philips, Juventus and The Economist.
markets: Holdings operate worldwide across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: Already tied to F1 as Ferrari's largest shareholder; a separate sponsorship by the holding itself is unlikely.
f1: Largest shareholder of Ferrari (about a quarter of shares), owner of the Scuderia Ferrari team

name: Itaú Unibanco
desc: Brazilian bank offering retail, corporate, investment and private banking, cards, insurance and asset management.
markets: Brazil core, with operations in Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Paraguay and Uruguay, plus international private banking offices.
rationale: Brazil's largest private bank and big sports sponsor; São Paulo GP and Latin American fans support a strong case.

name: CIMB Group
desc: Malaysian universal bank offering consumer, commercial, investment and Islamic banking across South-East Asia.
markets: Malaysia, Indonesia (CIMB Niaga), Singapore, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.
rationale: ASEAN consumer bank with sports sponsorship; Singapore Grand Prix gives a regional hospitality fit.

name: NCR Voyix
desc: Provider of point-of-sale, self-checkout, payments and store software for restaurants and retailers.
markets: Restaurant and retail customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B retail technology vendor; F1 hospitality could reach merchant clients but brand fit is modest.
changed: Renamed NCR Voyix after spinning off ATM business NCR Atleos in 2023

name: Nuvei
desc: Payments technology company providing card acquiring, local payment methods and payouts to e-commerce, gaming, travel and retail merchants.
markets: Merchants in over 200 markets across North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Payments brand serving gaming and online merchants; rivals Stripe and Visa sponsor F1, giving a B2B case.
changed: Taken private by Advent International in 2024

name: Ledger
desc: Maker of hardware cryptocurrency wallets such as Ledger Nano and Stax, plus the Ledger Live app and enterprise custody.
markets: Sells devices to crypto holders worldwide, with enterprise clients in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Crypto brands are active F1 sponsors; a premium security product fits F1's tech-focused audience.

name: CMC Markets
desc: Online trading company offering CFDs, spread betting, forex and stockbroking, plus white-label trading technology.
markets: Clients in the UK, Europe, Australia, Singapore and other Asian markets, with hubs in Sydney and Singapore.
rationale: Rival brokers such as Pepperstone, IC Markets and eToro sponsor F1, so the category fit is clear.

name: Thunes
desc: Cross-border payments network linking banks, mobile wallets and payment providers for transfers to wallets, accounts and cards.
markets: Payout network spanning over 130 countries in Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas; clients are fintechs and platforms.
rationale: B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand; F1 fit limited to client hospitality.

name: Phantom
desc: Self-custody crypto wallet app and browser extension for Solana, Ethereum, Bitcoin and other chains, with swaps and staking.
markets: Users worldwide online; no verified figures on its main markets or expansion plans.
rationale: Crypto peers sponsor F1 and its users are young and tech-focused, making F1 a plausible awareness play.

name: Sun Life Financial
desc: Insurer and wealth manager selling life and health insurance, retirement and asset management to individuals and employers.
markets: Canada, the US, several Asian markets and the UK.
rationale: Canadian and Asian consumer brand with sports sponsorship; Canadian GP and Asian races offer a plausible fit.

name: Futu Holdings
desc: Online brokerage running the Futubull and moomoo trading apps, with margin financing and wealth management services.
markets: Hong Kong and mainland Chinese clients, plus moomoo in the US, Singapore, Australia, Canada, Japan and Malaysia.
rationale: Retail trading brand expanding internationally; rival brokers sponsor F1, and Asian and US races fit its markets.

name: Xero
desc: Cloud accounting software company selling subscription accounting, payroll and payments tools to small businesses and accountants.
markets: New Zealand, Australia, the UK, US and other markets; US growth boosted by the Melio acquisition.
rationale: SME software brand with sports sponsorship; F1 could support US and UK awareness, though fit is moderate.
changed: Acquired Melio in 2025

name: bolttech
desc: Insurtech whose platform lets telecoms, retailers and banks sell device protection and other embedded insurance at the point of sale.
markets: Operates in more than 30 markets across Asia, Europe and the US.
rationale: Mostly B2B2C with limited consumer brand; F1 could support partner hospitality, but fit is moderate.

name: Paysend
desc: Money transfer fintech whose app lets consumers send money internationally to cards, accounts and wallets.
markets: Consumers sending money to about 160 countries; no verified detail on main sending markets.
rationale: Consumer remittance brand with sports sponsorship use; F1 gives broad reach, a plausible but not obvious fit.

name: XTB
desc: Online broker offering forex and CFD trading, stocks and ETFs through its xStation platform to retail clients.
markets: Poland and other European markets, with presence in Latin America and the Middle East.
rationale: Rival brokers already sponsor F1 and XTB uses sports marketing; European expansion supports a strong case.

name: IG Group
desc: Online trading and investing provider offering spread betting, CFDs, share dealing, options and crypto trading.
markets: Clients in the UK, Europe, the US through tastytrade, Australia, Singapore, Japan and other markets.
rationale: Former F1 team partner; rival brokers sponsor F1 now, so the category fit is strong.
changed: Acquired tastytrade in 2021

name: Nium
desc: Payment infrastructure company providing cross-border payouts, card issuing and wallets via API to banks, fintechs and businesses.
markets: Clients and licences across Asia-Pacific, Europe and North America; payouts to over 100 countries.
rationale: B2B fintech with limited consumer awareness; F1 relevant mainly for travel-payments clients and hospitality.
changed: Rebranded from Instarem to Nium in 2019

name: Plus500
desc: Online trading company offering CFDs, share dealing, futures and options to retail traders.
markets: Retail traders in Europe, the UK, Australia, Singapore and the US futures market.
rationale: Large sports sponsor whose broker rivals are on the F1 roster; strong category fit.

name: Adyen
desc: Payments company providing one platform for online, in-store and mobile payment acceptance, acquiring and issuing for large merchants.
markets: Merchants across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and Latin America.
rationale: Enterprise payments brand competing with F1 partners Stripe and Visa; tech showcase and hospitality fit.

name: Indian Oil Corporation
desc: State-controlled Indian oil company running refineries, pipelines, petrochemicals and India's largest fuel station network.
markets: India; small subsidiaries in Sri Lanka, Mauritius and the UAE; no major international marketing.
rationale: Huge Indian consumer brand and sports sponsor, but no Indian GP and domestic focus limit F1 value.

name: Reliance Industries
desc: Indian conglomerate in oil refining and petrochemicals, retail, Jio telecoms and digital services, media and new energy.
markets: Mostly Indian consumers; refined products and petrochemicals exported worldwide.
rationale: Very strong Indian brand owner with cricket sponsorship; F1 fit depends on international ambitions, which remain limited.

name: Cheniere Energy
desc: Largest US exporter of liquefied natural gas, operating Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi terminals under long-term contracts.
markets: Sells LNG to utilities and traders in Europe, Asia and Latin America from US terminals.
rationale: B2B energy company with no consumer brand; F1 useful only for buyer hospitality, a weak fit.

name: Naturgy
desc: Spanish gas and electricity utility supplying customers, operating networks, renewable generation and LNG supply.
markets: Spain core, with operations in Latin America including Mexico, Chile, Argentina and Brazil, plus global LNG trading.
rationale: Consumer energy brand in Spain and Mexico; Spanish and Mexican races give a plausible fit for a utility.
changed: Renamed from Gas Natural Fenosa in 2018

name: QatarEnergy
desc: State oil and gas company of Qatar producing LNG, oil, petrochemicals and fertilisers, with international upstream and LNG stakes.
markets: LNG buyers in Asia and Europe; stakes in projects in the US, Africa, Latin America and elsewhere.
rationale: Qatar hosts a Grand Prix and Qatar Airways and Visit Qatar are F1 partners; strong national fit.
changed: Renamed from Qatar Petroleum in 2021

name: Vedanta
desc: Indian natural resources group producing zinc, silver, aluminium, copper, iron ore, oil and gas and power.
markets: Mainly India, with mining operations in South Africa and Namibia and metals sold to global buyers.
rationale: Mainly B2B commodity producer with little consumer marketing; F1 fit is weak beyond occasional corporate hospitality.

name: Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC)
desc: State energy group of Abu Dhabi producing oil and gas, with refining, petrochemicals, gas processing and fuel retail.
markets: Exports oil, gas and chemicals worldwide; investments abroad through XRG and other units.
rationale: Abu Dhabi hosts the season finale and the state backs Etihad's F1 deals; strong national hospitality fit.

name: Petrobras
desc: Brazilian state-controlled oil and gas company producing mainly deep-water pre-salt crude, with refining and gas.
markets: Mainly Brazil; exports crude to Asia, Europe and the Americas.
rationale: Former McLaren partner and big Brazilian sponsor; São Paulo GP hospitality makes F1 plausible.

name: Woodside Energy
desc: Australian oil and gas producer supplying LNG and oil from Australia, the Gulf of Mexico and other assets.
markets: Production in Australia, the US Gulf of Mexico and Trinidad and Tobago; LNG customers in Asia and Europe.
rationale: B2B energy producer with limited consumer brand; Australian GP hospitality is the main angle, so weak.
changed: Merged with BHP's petroleum business in 2022
